item.title: PS5's September 2026 Console Update Adds Widget That May Be a Game Changer
item.description:
A new PS5 system software update went live on September 16, bringing a new widget to the Welcome Hub that shows users which PS5 titles are popular in a given region. The PS5 system update is now available in the US and Canada, with a gradual rollout throughout the globe.

PlayStation periodically releases firmware updates to ensure system stability and security as time goes on. Some updates also include new features that players can utilize on their PlayStation console, such as new widgets or wallpapers for the Welcome Hub. The PS5 system update released in late July 2026 was a case of the latter. Sony stated that messages and usability on some screens were improved in the July update, but the company did not delve into any further details about these changes.

Disco Elysium Successor Officially Coming to PS5 on November 3

The follow-up to ZA/UM's Disco Elysium is finally heading to PlayStation 5 with its release date officially confirmed for November 3.

By Drew Swanson

PS5's Latest Update Adds a Nifty Trending Games Widget

After an August beta test period, some new features are now available for PlayStation users to peruse. The update introduced the "Community Activity" widget to the Welcome Hub. The widget shows which PS5 games are trending within a user's home region, along with the 10 most popular PS5 games in a week. As of this writing, Fortnite , Minecraft , and Grand Theft Auto 5 topped the weekly PS5 charts in the US, while games like NHL 27 and Teardown were trending titles. The new update also introduced an option that will display the PSN username of whoever is speaking in a voice chat. The name display's position can also be adjusted. Users must connect to the Internet and download PS5 system update version 26.06-14.00.00 onto their console to use these new features.

The September PS5 update also made a change that only PS5 Pro users will see. The Enhance PSSR Image Quality option on PS5 Pro is now automatically active by default. Additionally, any game that supports the previous iteration of PlayStation's upscaling technology will work with the enhanced PSSR option. Users can turn this off within the Video Output menu in the system's Settings. An option to turn off Bluetooth functionality across the entire PS5 console has been added, which will also disable HDMI Device Link and rest mode. Sony cautioned that turning off Bluetooth should only be used at esports venues as a way to manage controller connections during an event.

The new console update came amid a busy week for PlayStation gamers, as Marvel's Wolverine hit store shelves just one day beforehand. As the latest title by Insomniac Games, Wolverine is a gritty action game featuring the titular antihero of Marvel’s X-Men comics. However, reception to the latest PS5 exclusive has been mixed, with criticism pointed at the game's combat depth and navigation mechanics. Insomniac stated it would remain receptive to player feedback, though it is unclear what post-launch changes the studio has planned.

PS5's September 2026 Console Update Adds Widget That May Be a Game Changer
Diablo 5 Officially Confirms Baldur’s Gate 3 Feature
Lies of P May Have Found the Perfect Way to Turn One Soulslike Into a Franchise
5 Perfect 10/10 FPS Masterpieces Nobody Remembers

However, the current news cycle has been far from rosy for Sony. The company's ongoing push toward digital exclusivity led some gamers to protest the decision. In response, PlayStation doubled down by sending an email that stated all digital games on its platform were a license that did not grant users individual ownership of a game.

PS5 System Software Version 26.06-14.00.00 Update Notes (September 16, 2026)

  • We've turned on Enhance PSSR Image Quality as a default setting. When you update the system software, this setting automatically turns on. When you enable this feature, enhanced PSSR is used even for games that support the previous version of PSSR, so you can enjoy a sharper and clearer visual experience.
    • To turn off this setting, go to Settings > Screen and Video > Video Output > Enhance PSSR Image Quality.
    • This feature is available only on PS5 Pro.

  • You can now see who’s speaking while you’re in a voice chat.
    • To show the speaker indicator, go to the voice chat card in the control center. Select More > Display Who’s Speaking and turn on Display Names.
    • To choose where the speaker indicator appears on your screen, select Position.

  • We’ve added the Community Activity widget to your Welcome Hub. You can switch between the following views.
    • Trending Now displays ten multiplayer games or multiplayer modes that are surging in popularity. Look here for new game releases or games with major content updates.
    • Top 10 displays the ten most popular games in the last week for your country or region. Look here to see what games have a large community of players you can join.

  • We’ve changed the following features for PS5 consoles and PS5 Pro consoles in certain countries or regions.
    • If you go to Settings > Accessories > General > Advanced Settings and select Turn Off Bluetooth, your console does not enter rest mode and HDMI Device Link does not function.
    • The Turn Off Bluetooth function is for managing controller connections at esports venues and similar locations. Do not use this feature for any other purpose.

  • We've improved system software performance and stability.

item.title: Battle.net Is Becoming Something Blizzard Says It Doesn't Want to Be
item.description:
BlizzCon has come and gone, and with it, we got reveals for basically every Blizzard IP out there, from World of Warcraft to Overwatch , but in between all the big announcements were a few equally interesting ones that no-one saw coming. We already knew that The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered was coming to Battle.net in late September, but it is being joined by Cyberpunk 2077 later in the year, which has a lot of players excited, yet it raises a question regarding the platform's place in the wider gaming market.

Over the years, Battle.net has grown from Blizzard 's exclusive launcher for all their games across several generations into a strange mix of first-party titles and games from other studios, primarily driven by Xbox's acquisition of the company back in 2023. When you boot up the launcher, you see the classic names like Diablo and StarCraft , but are now greeted with Avowed , The Outer Worlds 2 , and soon, the CD Projekt Red heavy hitters, which starts to make it look less like a Blizzard-only space and more like a universal platform. And, while it is clear that Blizzard isn't going to overtake Steam or even Epic Games overnight, it raises the question about where Battle.net fits in the conversation about gaming launchers, especially as more big names are added over time.

The Witcher 3 Remastered May Have Found What Modern Remasters Are Missing

The Witcher 3 Remastered already proves that with enough consideration and intention, modern remakes and remasters can be unambiguously player-first.

By Christopher Adams

Blizzard Is Adding Two Massive RPGs to Its Library on Battle.net

Just over a decade ago, Battle.net was a platform reserved for Blizzard's games and content, and although it had nowhere near as many games as something like Steam, quantity was far from the point. In my eyes, the launcher stood as the main hub for all things Blizzard, and it didn't matter if you came for WoW or Starcraft ; the platform had a very specific reason to exist. As time has gone on, we have seen more games being added to the platform, with sequels launching and several spin-offs rounding out the edges, but the list that exists now is far from Blizzard-dominated.

You can use Battle.net to launch the latest Call of Duty , or sail the oceans in Sea of Thieves , and now you are going to be able to play two of the greatest single-player RPGs ever made, with Cyberpunk 2077 and The Witcher 3 joining the fray. Now some of the additions make sense from a corporate point of view, because of the relationship between Activision and Blizzard, but these large RPGs also feel like an ideal fit for the platform. If you already have a big player base of RPG lovers who may be looking for something new, then why not give them exactly what they want on their doorstep, instead of forcing them to look elsewhere in the competition?

And, while it is clear that Blizzard isn't going to overtake Steam or even Epic Games overnight, it raises the question about where Battle.net fits in the conversation about gaming launchers, especially as more big names are added over time.

However, when you begin adding more and more games to a launcher, it starts to look less like a tailored list and more like a fully-fleshed out gaming platform. Blizzard themselves have said that these additions are in no way intended to make Battle.net compete with Steam or Epic Games, and the focused approach is intended to give the existing players on the platform the kinds of games that they think would be the best fit (via GamesRadar). I do see the argument, as it isn't as if Blizzard has opened the floodgates and added any and all games to their platform and is instead taking things slow with a more structured set of deals.

At the same time, it gets to a point where the cross-over between platforms becomes hard to avoid. Sure, if you have a single or a couple of games, then you aren't exactly sharing much space with Steam, but if you then end up with 50+, with more on the way, then those strategic partnerships with your existing games look less like nice fits for the platform and more like an attempt to take up market space. What's more is that if you have the same games available across a range of different platforms, it adds an extra burden on both you, the publisher, and the consumer. You need to think about platform deals and competing prices and even bundles, and conversely, consumers have to do a lot more shopping around and might just settle for the simplest solution, which is almost always wherever they have the most games.

When Platforms Collide

It's no secret that there is some serious competition in the world of gaming platforms. For consoles, it is a little more black and white, as you are choosing both the hardware and the platform at the same time, but for PC, you have access to dozens of different launchers and publishers all in one place, so the choice about where to buy becomes a lot more complex. Games like Sea of Thieves are a great example of this, as, because the game is published by Xbox Game Studios, you can actually access it in far more places than you might expect, from Battle.net to Steam, and of course, Xbox's own launcher.

The latter of the bunch is the most interesting, as there already exists some very real friction between Xbox's acquired platforms. Blizzard sits under their umbrella, and so you have access to things like Warcraft 3 and Overwatch in the Xbox PC app, but other games like World of Warcraft are still stuck with Battle.net. And, because of the need for account linking, cross-progression, and multiple update points, it can be a lot more frustrating to swap back and forth when compared to other platforms like Steam, and that assumes you can even do that to begin with.

But, if the plan is to expand the Battle.net platform with these RPGs that many people are still yet to play, then you would assume that the publishers want you to stick around in one place for longer, as opposed to having your library with someone else. However, there is a further contradiction within the Blizzard/Xbox world, as while the former still operates under its own control, the crossovers between the two are looking increasingly strange from the outside.

For example, if I play Diablo IV on the Xbox PC app, then I still need to go through Battle.net, and the same goes for other Blizzard titles on Game Pass. Then, if I buy Avowed , I will again have access to it in both stores, and I might continue to buy more games on the Xbox Store to pad out my library, track my achievements, etc. Then, I see that The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 are coming to Battle.net, and I scurry to preorder them, only to see that they aren't also present on Xbox. That means I have to choose where to play my games yet again, and if I see that Steam has all of those games plus thousands more, then I might as well keep Battle.net around for occasional WoW sessions, and stick to the larger platform for my singleplayer adventures.

Battle.net Is Becoming Something Blizzard Says It Doesn't Want to Be
Everything Officially Confirmed About Diablo 5
Diablo 4 Players Can Claim A Free In-Game Item For A Limited Time
Diablo 4 Season 15 Officially Delayed at the Last Minute [UPDATE]

This exact scenario has been happening for years now, and the universal outcome is almost always to go with a single platform that houses the majority of your games. If Blizzard wants to have some of their partnered games on Battle.net, then I see no issue, as it makes sense to keep all your names under the same roof. However, the claim that by adding other third-party games you aren't competing with other platforms is strictly false and plays into the same old question of why would someone buy their games on X if they already own them on Y. I expect that Blizzard is preparing for the future, establishing Battle.net as a place for later titles like The Witcher 4 and potentially more RPGs down the line. But I also know that people universally hate using more platforms than they need to, with the EA app being a perfect case study, so I still fail to see a world where these partnerships expand much further, unless Battle.net gets absorbed into the Xbox app.

item.title: 9-Year-Old Minecraft Player Racks Up Over $100,000 on Dad's Credit Card
item.description:
A 9-year-old Minecraft player has reportedly spent over $100,000 on their father's credit card. The discovery came as a major shock, and now the young Minecraft fan is in significant hot water.

Myriads of Minecraft players have plenty of fun with the game without ever opening their wallets. There are optional purchases that fans can make to add new content and cosmetics, but ultimately, the core game keeps many players satisfied, and Minecraft mods can help to further expand the game without spending more. However, this particular case didn't actually involve handing money directly to Minecraft .

The 31 Weirdest Minecraft Seeds

Minecraft features countless maps that players can start in, but for those looking for some weird seeds, these are the best to check out.

4
By Aly Azmy

Minecraft Player Digs a Deep Debt Hole

A young Minecraft fan got the idea of uploading gameplay of his playthroughs after watching YouTube streamers. It started out innocently, with the child sharing footage on a channel called Mighty Mike Plays, with permission from his father. However, he's now in serious trouble after racking up over $100,000 in credit card bills. His father, David Sarkisyan, has taken over the YouTube channel and explained in a video that it is shutting down, at least temporarily, after he was made aware of massive charges on his company's credit card. Unfortunately, the father apparently made a grave mistake of using the company card to help promote the child's YouTube account. What started out as a humble $20 ad spend quickly grew out of control after the child went in after the fact and removed the limit. Unfortunately, this has also led to the child's father getting in serious trouble at work, with the impact on his employment yet to be determined.

David claims that the insane amount of money spent on the advertising campaign was kept completely secret from him. Under normal circumstances, a credit card would have a limit on how much could be spent, and would likely alert the cardholder to the massive charges long before they'd reached this point. However, due to it being a company credit card, the card was essentially unlimited, and the charges supposedly went unnoticed for three weeks. While it's far from the first time that a kid has spent tons of money on games without their parents' permission or knowledge, the company card makes this a rather unique situation.

David has said that some kind of punishment is in order for his child, but surprisingly, isn't as angry about it as one might expect. He notes in the video that he isn't blaming the child for what happened, saying that the kid didn't fully understand that the advertising campaign used real money. That same claim has been made by some other kids who have spent their parents' money on video games without permission, though several people in the comments section are expressing disbelief, saying that a 9-year-old is more than old enough to understand financial responsibility. However, utilizing a company credit card for a personal purchase like this was undoubtedly a mistake that David won't be making again in the future.

Diablo 5 Officially Confirms Baldur’s Gate 3 Feature

Some responding to the video have expressed doubt about the whole thing, with some wondering if it's an elaborate ruse to drum up attention for the channel. If that were the case, it's certainly worked, as the Mighty Mike Plays channel has exploded in subscribers and views, with over 62,000 subscribers and over half a million views on the dad's video thus far. If nothing else, it's a good reminder to use parental controls in games and online, and to not use anything but a personal credit card for personal purposes like this one.

However, he's now in serious trouble after racking up over $100,000 in credit card bills. His father, David Sarkisyan, has taken over the YouTube channel and explained in a video that it is shutting down, at least temporarily, after he was made aware of massive charges on his company's credit card. Unfortunately, the father apparently made a grave mistake of using the company card to help promote the child's YouTube account. What started out as a humble $20 ad spend quickly grew out of control after the child went in after the fact and removed the limit. Unfortunately, this has also led to the child's father getting in serious trouble at work, with the impact on his employment yet to be determined.

David claims that the insane amount of money spent on the advertising campaign was kept completely secret from him. Under normal circumstances, a credit card would have a limit on how much could be spent, and would likely alert the cardholder to the massive charges long before they'd reached this point. However, due to it being a company credit card, the card was essentially unlimited, and the charges supposedly went unnoticed for three weeks. While it's far from the first time that a kid has spent tons of money on games without their parents' permission or knowledge, the company card makes this a rather unique situation.

David has said that some kind of punishment is in order for his child, but surprisingly, isn't as angry about it as one might expect. He notes in the video that he isn't blaming the child for what happened, saying that the kid didn't fully understand that the advertising campaign used real money. That same claim has been made by some other kids who have spent their parents' money on video games without permission, though several people in the comments section are expressing disbelief, saying that a 9-year-old is more than old enough to understand financial responsibility. However, utilizing a company credit card for a personal purchase like this was undoubtedly a mistake that David won't be making again in the future.

item.title: What To Do With Starine in Aniimo
item.description:
Starine might be one of the first materials players can collect in Aniimo , and looking at their description, it seems to be linked to a mysterious nest in the Forest of Falling Stars . But what should Pathfinders do with this star-shaped fruit? The answer is a bit tricky, since Starine is also an Evolution Material needed to progress the Celestis Line, so, first and foremost, we need to discover what to do with it, and where's this mysterious place named in the description. Here's what to do with Starine in Aniimo .

Which Free Prismana To Choose in Aniimo

Which free Prismana to choose in Aniimo? First Starter Choice Explained and Prismana Aniimo Guide.

By Lucas Simons

How To Find Mysterious Nest in Forest of Falling Stars

The Forest of Falling Stars is located directly North of the first Outpost players visit in Idyll (follow a straight line from the Bloom and you'll find it), and if they are already around level 20 , they can unlock a special Investigation quest that will help them unlock the Celestis Evolution Line.

The first thing they need to do is to collect at least 20 Starine , and travel to the place marked on the map below. Next, players should have a Celestis on their party , so they can Twine with it .

Once players are there, they will find a location called ' Nest of Stars.' Its all the way following the stream, so you cannot miss it. Now, Twine with Celestis to enter their nest and notice there are 3 big Nests right in front of the entrance.

Interacting with them will reveal you need Big Starine , a material that is only available in this area. The first one is located to the right of the cave, inside a fallen trunk.

The second Big Starine is located on the left side , protected by a Celestis that will ask players for 10 Starine in exchange for the Big Starine . So, hand out the Starine and claim the second Big Starine.

The third one is located floating near the Star Tree , and players need to climb the pillars then glide down with Celestis to make it fall to the ground and then, pick it up.

With the three Big Starine in your power go to the nest and deposit them to summon Stellarys. After that a Star Fall will begin and all the Celestis will gather to celebrate.

As a reward, players will receive various Evolution Materials, including the rare Treasured Large Starine a quest item you need to take to Parfumer Dael to create a powerful item called Peace of Mind you will need to progress further down your Training Paths, by completing A Fragant Journey: Forest of Falling Stars.

With that, players will conclude one of the goals of their Elite Training Goals, which is required to level up their Pathfinder Levels, and raise the level cap of both player and Aniimo alike.

This also unlocks the Alpha Aniimo (Boss Fight) in Forest of Falling Stars , so head there and beat Stellarys , and make sure to catch it since you only have one chance to get it after beating it. (Use special grade Aniipods -Aniipod Ultra- to catch it at a 100% rate).

Starine does have another use: It is used as Evolution Material, to raise the level of Celestis Family Aniimo (including Stellarys). players will need to use it to level up their Celestis without having to rely on combat. It can also be used to sell for credits in the inventory.

Now, if your Celestis has reaches level 18, after beating Stellarys, you can technically evolve it. You will also require a material called Night Stone, which is required for all Dark-type Aniimo.

And that's about everything you need to know about Starine in Aniimo. Here are a few bonus tips for you:

  • Make sure to interact with all Celestis in the Nest of Stars to complete the Celestis Family Research.
  • Once the Star Tree is active, ride the updraft to a second hidden location on top of the Nest. Interact with the small nest there to increase your Research Level.
  • You can also enjoy a rest on the bench near the tree, and take some cool pictures.

item.title: Disney Dreamlight Valley Pulls Back the Curtain on New Free Update
item.description:
A new free update has been announced for Disney Dreamlight Valley , and developer Gameloft is bringing content that should appeal to players looking to celebrate Halloween. Since its early access launch in 2022, Disney Dreamlight Valley has received a steady stream of content, including free goodies for all players and paid DLC updates. This has given the developer opportunities to add several major characters spanning various Disney properties.

Disney Dreamlight Valley 's next paid expansion arrives in November, and it will add Jack Sparrow from Pirates of the Caribbean . The Keepsake Sea will take players on an adventure in the ocean, allowing them to grow fins and swim with Ariel, or explore with Milo from Atlantis: The Lost Empire . There are still a lot of details yet to be revealed, but Gameloft plans on divulging a lot more during a showcase on October 21.

Cozy Games You Can Play for 20 Minutes or 200 Hours

These cozy games offer a satisfying experience for those who only have a few minutes to play, but also feature hundreds of hours of content to explore

By Katelyn Mitchell Jewett

Disney Dreamlight Valley Reveals Season of Scares Update

On September 23 , Disney Dreamlight Valley will receive a new update known as Season of Scares. The big addition this time around is Oogie Boogie, the central antagonist from The Nightmare Before Christmas . Disney Dreamlight Valley previously added Jack and Sally, and Gameloft clearly isn't done with the film. In addition to Oogie Boogie, Season of Scares will be adding Zero as a companion. The update will include six weeks' worth of challenges, with different rewards for completing them. After the final week of challenges, players will be able to invite Oogie Boogie to join the Valley.

The arrival of Oogie Boogie was previously confirmed, and it was known that there would be a September update thanks to a previous Disney Dreamlight Valley roadmap. However, Gameloft has offered much more information about what to expect, including some interesting details about Oogie Boogie. For one thing, there is a time constraint tied to the character. Players must start his first quest prior to November 4 in order to add him to the Valley. If players miss the deadline, the character will return, but not until sometime around Halloween 2027. As long as players have started the first quest by that date, they will be able to complete the rest of the challenges at their own pace.

The limited-time nature of Oogie Boogie's arrival has already led to some frustration among players. The Nightmare Before Christmas is a hugely popular movie, and the idea of locking a character for those that miss the deadline is proving somewhat controversial. Hopefully, players that want Oogie Boogie in their Village won't have a problem starting the event before the end date, so they can make sure that they can see the villain interacting with Jack and Sally once again.

Fortnite Officially Reveals Kingdom Hearts Collab
Kingdom Hearts 4 Leaks Star Wars World and More
'I'm Pretty Sure I Mean It' Deus Ex, System Shock Creator Warren Spector Announces Retirement
Kingdom Hearts 4's Coco Reveal Just Put One Major Concern to Rest

Following Season of Scares, Disney Dreamlight Valley will have at least one more free update before the year comes to an end. Lilo will be added in an update set to be released in December, which will see the character reunited with her pal, Stitch. Stitch has been in Disney Dreamlight Valley for quite a while, but his best pal will finally make her debut. It's not unusual for Disney Dreamlight Valley to space out characters from the same movie or franchise, but it's safe to assume that a lot of players have wanted to see Lilo added to the game before this point.
